“Tell me, sir,” I said, “the names of the virgins and of the women dressed in black garments.”[a] “Listen,” he said, “to the names of the strongest virgins, those stationed at the corners.”

2. “The first is Faith, the second Self-Control, the third Power, and the fourth Patience. The others stationed between them have these names: Sincerity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Understanding, Harmony and Love. Whoever bears these names, along with the name of the Son of God, will be able to enter God’s kingdom.”

3. “Listen also,” he said, “to the names of the women wearing black garments. Four of these are more powerful: the first is Unbelief, the second Lack of Self-Control, the third Disobedience, and the fourth Deceit. Their followers are called Sorrow, Evil, Shamelessness, Quick Temper, Falsehood, Folly, Slander and Hatred.[b] A servant of God who bears these names[c] will see God’s kingdom, but will not enter it.”

4. “Sir,” I said, “who are the stones from the depths that have been fitted into the building?” “The first ten, laid in the foundations,” he said, “are the first generation. The twenty-five are the second generation of righteous people. The thirty-five are God’s prophets and his servants. The forty are apostles and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God.”[d]

5. “Why, then, sir,” I said, “did the virgins also hand over these stones for the building of the tower, after carrying them through the gate?”

6. “Because these people were the first to wear these spirits,” he said, “and they never parted from one another at all: neither the spirits from the people nor the people from the spirits. The spirits remained with them until they fell asleep.[e] If they had not had these spirits with them, they would not have been useful for building this tower.”[f]

old.text: The printed opening has restorations in damaged Athos and a bar-marked insertion asking about the black-clothed women and repeating the request for the virgins’ names. The apparatus attributes the insertion to Gebhardt, compared with the Latin traditions. Sinaiticus also preserves part of the request about the women; its “black” is wholly supplied and “garments” partly supplied in the primary XML. It cannot certify the complete inserted opening as intact text.

These are names of allegorical figures. “Sorrow” translates Lype within the vice list; it does not classify every experience of grief as sinful. “Shamelessness” can also be rendered “licentiousness.” The names preserve the two groups of twelve and the stated order.

The printed working text says “these names”; Sinaiticus says “these spirits” in this sentence. Alternative: “A servant of God who bears these spirits will see God’s kingdom, but will not enter it.” The draft keeps the working names reading and exposes the spirit terminology; the kingdom contrast is not softened.
The source gives ten, twenty-five, thirty-five and forty, without naming individual people. “Servants” here renders diakonoi; no later church office or complete list of forty apostles is supplied.
“Fell asleep” is the source’s expression for death in this context, as the following chapter makes explicit. The people are not described as merely taking an ordinary sleep.

The printed Athos-based text reconstructs the negative “would not” in damage. Several neighboring words are partly restored. It supports the negative sense without certifying every letter as surviving ink.

theological_decisions:
- issue: Bearing names and spirits, kingdom entry, and fitness for the tower
  chosen_reading: Retain the statement that whoever bears the virgins’ names and the name of the Son of
    God will be able to enter God’s kingdom, and that a servant of God bearing the women’s names will
    see the kingdom but will not enter it. Preserve the stone groups, their enduring relationship with
    the spirits until death, and the final negative conditional stating that without these spirits they
    would not have been useful for building the tower.
  rationale: The Greek distinguishes ability to enter the kingdom from seeing it without entering, identifies
    the stone groups, and describes the people and spirits remaining together until the people’s death.
    Do not soften the exclusion or the final necessity claim. Preserve the disclosed names/spirits variant
    and the editorial supply in the final negative conditional.

translation:
  text: '“Sir,” I said, “tell me the names of the virgins and the women dressed in black.”[a] He said,
    “Listen to the names of the strongest virgins, who stood at the corners.”


    2. “The first is Faith, the second Self-Control, the third Power, and the fourth Patience. Those standing
    between them are Sincerity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Understanding, Harmony and Love.
    Whoever bears these names and the name of the Son of God will be able to enter God’s kingdom.”


    3. He said, “Now listen to the names of the women dressed in black. Four are more powerful: Unbelief,
    Lack of Self-Control, Disobedience and Deceit. Their followers are Sorrow, Evil, Shamelessness, Quick
    Temper, Falsehood, Folly, Slander and Hatred.[b] A servant of God who bears these names[c] will see
    God’s kingdom, but will not enter it.”


    4. “Sir,” I said, “who are the stones from the depths that were fitted into the building?” He said,
    “The first ten stones laid in the foundations are the first generation. The twenty-five are the second
    generation of righteous people. The thirty-five are God’s prophets and servants. The forty are apostles
    and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God.”[d]


    5. “Then why, sir,” I said, “did the virgins carry these stones too through the gate and hand them
    over for building the tower?”


    6. He said, “These people were the first to wear these spirits. The people and spirits never parted
    from each other. The spirits stayed with the people until they fell asleep.[e] Without these spirits,
    they would not have been useful for building this tower.”[f]'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The printed opening has restorations in damaged Athos and a bar-marked insertion asking about
      the black-clothed women and repeating the request for the virgins’ names. The apparatus attributes
      the insertion to Gebhardt, compared with the Latin traditions. Sinaiticus also preserves part of
      the request about the women; its “black” is wholly supplied and “garments” partly supplied in the
      primary XML. It cannot certify the complete inserted opening as intact text.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: These are names of allegorical figures. “Sorrow” translates Lype within the vice list; it does
      not classify every experience of grief as sinful. “Shamelessness” can also be rendered “licentiousness.”
      The names preserve the two groups of twelve and the stated order.
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The printed working text says “these names”; Sinaiticus says “these spirits” in this sentence.
      Alternative: “A servant of God who bears these spirits will see God’s kingdom, but will not enter
      it.” The draft keeps the working names reading and exposes the spirit terminology; the kingdom contrast
      is not softened.'
  - marker: d
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The source gives ten, twenty-five, thirty-five and forty, without naming individual people.
      “Servants” here renders diakonoi; no later church office or complete list of forty apostles is supplied.
  - marker: e
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: “Fell asleep” is the source’s expression for death in this context, as the following chapter
      makes explicit. The people are not described as merely taking an ordinary sleep.
  - marker: f
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The printed Athos-based text reconstructs the negative “would not” in damage. The primary Sinaiticus
      transcription,Q95F8r col3 lines27–32, has the negative conditional, including ou[k] an: the k is
      supplied, not the entire negative. Several neighboring words are partly restored. It supports the
      negative sense without certifying every letter as surviving ink.'

base_translation:
  text: '“Tell me, sir,” I said, “the names of the virgins and of the women dressed in black garments.”[a]
    “Listen,” he said, “to the names of the strongest virgins, those stationed at the corners.”


    2. “The first is Faith, the second Self-Control, the third Power, and the fourth Patience. The others
    stationed between them have these names: Sincerity, Innocence, Purity, Cheerfulness, Truth, Understanding,
    Harmony and Love. Whoever bears these names, along with the name of the Son of God, will be able to
    enter God’s kingdom.”


    3. “Listen also,” he said, “to the names of the women wearing black garments. Four of these are more
    powerful: the first is Unbelief, the second Lack of Self-Control, the third Disobedience, and the
    fourth Deceit. Their followers are called Sorrow, Evil, Shamelessness, Quick Temper, Falsehood, Folly,
    Slander and Hatred.[b] A servant of God who bears these names[c] will see God’s kingdom, but will
    not enter it.”


    4. “Sir,” I said, “who are the stones from the depths that have been fitted into the building?” “The
    first ten, laid in the foundations,” he said, “are the first generation. The twenty-five are the second
    generation of righteous people. The thirty-five are God’s prophets and his servants. The forty are
    apostles and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God.”[d]


    5. “Why, then, sir,” I said, “did the virgins also hand over these stones for the building of the
    tower, after carrying them through the gate?”


    6. “Because these people were the first to wear these spirits,” he said, “and they never parted from
    one another at all: neither the spirits from the people nor the people from the spirits. The spirits
    remained with them until they fell asleep.[e] If they had not had these spirits with them, they would
    not have been useful for building this tower.”[f]'
